copy.blurb:
The model fancies Egypt more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Belgium. +8.9pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Elo numbers going in: Belgium 1860, Egypt 1760. That's a 100-point lead for Belgium — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 49%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 27%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Egypt sits at 27% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 59%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 18%. On the Egypt side specifically the market reads 18%, which prices out at American odds of +441. Compared against the model's 27%, that's the +8.9pp gap the Pick rests on.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Egypt side that lower bound is 22% — +3.9pp clear of the market's 18%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 27 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Egypt a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +8.9pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On Egypt, the model is +8.9pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 27%; the market reads 18%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: Belgium v Egypt · the model leans Egypt
